TITLE: Consensus-Based 3D Colorization
PROPOSAL: Develop Consensus-Based 3D Colorization, a novel method that combines multiple 2D colorization models, each trained on individual viewpoints or patches of the same scene, and aggregates their predictions through a voting system that prevents information loss and promotes consensus.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Image1, Baseline: Voting-Based 2D Colorization, Ablation: Single-Model Colorization, Ablation: Voting without consensus threshold
COST: 10,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Consensus-Based 3D Colorization could achieve high-quality and consistent colorization across views, but may struggle with scenes containing uniform or solid colors where consenus will be difficult to determine.

title: building the first controllable 3d colorizer for dynamic scenes
PROPOSAL: Investigate a novel neural architecture that combines the strengths of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and user-guided implicit methods for controllable 3D colorization. Specifically, extend NeRF with a module that can dynamically learn and adjust color palettes based on user-provided guidance (e.g. text prompts, reference images). The goal is to enable the model to produce temporally coherent and consistent colors across multiple views while allowing for user control over the final output.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed architecture with a baseline NeRF model that does not include user-guided colorization, and evaluate its performance using metrics such as photorealism, color consistency, and user satisfaction.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed architecture should improve the overall quality of the 3D colorization output, enabling more realistic and temporally consistent colors while providing users with a higher degree of control over the final result.

TITLE: exploring content-preserving multi-view image comparison
PROPOSAL: Incorporate a spatial consistency loss objective into the comparison metric to assess the similarity between colorized images from different views. COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed spatial consistency loss objective should improve the performance of the comparison metric, leading to more coherent and consistent colorizations across views.

title: proposed approach: locally aware multi-view 2d colorization
PROPOSAL: Train a collection of 2D colorization models, each applied to a fixed viewpoint or local region of the monochromatic input images. This can leverage existing architectures, pre-trained on large color image datasets like COCO-Stuff. For local regions where the colorizer struggles, additionally use a separate module for distilling color consistency across views via an attention mechanism. This method would allow control over local color regions and improve its robustness against viewpoint changes.
CONTROLS: Implement four baselines: (1) state-of-the-art colorization models (such as AlexNet-based Pixel2Pix), (2) the state-of-the-art for dynamic scenes (a combination of different colorizers that operate in patches), (3) the overly simplified single global colorizer, and (4) patchwise color averaging as a performance baseline.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Locally aware multi-view 2D colorization will improve the consistency of colors across views at specific regions, while patchwise color averaging will still cause color shifts and losses of detailed information. However, patch averaging is likely to outperform the simplistically fragmented single global colorizer, showing the necessity of more sophisticated 2D color models.
